title: 16th Sitting of first Session of 2025
summary: The Majlis sent the President's Supreme Court nominee to the Judiciary Committee, heard the first reading of a resolution on government spending against the 2025 budget, and took two committee reports. The ministry-restructuring report drew no speakers. A debate on a Rules of Procedure change to shorten committee deadlines turned into a sharp exchange between government and opposition members, including over the separation of powers. Both reports were then approved by 50 votes to 0.

items.title: Opening of the sitting and prayer
Attendance of members
items.outcome: announced by the chair: 35 present, 10 on leave, 1 on official travel

items.title: President's nomination of Ustaz Hussain Shaheed as Supreme Court judge
items.outcome: letter read out; sent to the Judiciary Committee for review

items.title: Resolution by Dr Ahmed Shamheed on government and Maldives Monetary Authority actions against the passed 2025 budget
Government Accountability Committee report on the President's changes to ministry portfolios (Housing, Finance, Climate Change/Tourism)
General Committee report on Ahmed Naseer's amendment to the Majlis Rules of Procedure (art. 180)
Votes on items on the agenda
items.outcome: both committee reports approved, 50 yes, none against

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Thanked the committee but said ministers are not actually being summoned, citing Ramadan and a newspaper report.
Argued the Majlis now works under the President's control and that it passes laws on request.
Raised a point of order calling a claim made about him untrue.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said the Kendhoo member's claims were untrue and that the amendment came from a committee MDP members also voted for.
Accused opposition members of spreading false claims and urged them to stop actions he said harm the economy.
Explained the amendment shortens committee deadlines and thanked the Vaikaradhoo member for backing it.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Supported the report, calling it a historic decision that brings ministers' accountability closer to people's feelings.
Thanked Inguraidhoo's member for a correction and criticised opposition members for shouting on the floor.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Called the amendment important and useful for speeding committee work and giving services to citizens sooner.
Raised a point of order on the period for summoning ministers, saying it was not changed.

speakers.name: Adam Zahir
positions: Presented the committee report recommending the Majlis approve the President's changes to ministry portfolios; the committee's members present agreed unanimously.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Presented the General Committee report backing the Rules amendment, saying it would speed up committee work and make committees more transparent.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Point of order: the presidency and the Majlis are separate branches; one does not control the other.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported the amendment, saying delays in summoning ministers frustrate the public, and criticised opposition conduct and past governments' record.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Said his MDP colleagues supported the report, and complained of getting no reply to a written question to the Defence Minister on Indian troops.

decisions: President's Supreme Court nominee Hussain Shaheed referred to the Judiciary Committee for review.
First reading held for Dr Ahmed Shamheed's resolution on government and MMA actions against the 2025 budget.
Amendment to the Majlis Rules of Procedure (Ahmed Naseer) approved 50-0.
Next sitting set for 19 March 2025 at 10:30.

votes.what: Approve the President's changes to ministry portfolios (Construction, Housing and Infrastructure; Finance and Planning; Tourism and Environment)
Approve Ahmed Naseer's amendment to the Majlis Rules of Procedure as recommended by the General Committee
